**First-touch grading** (seat `repo:objectui`; session `session_01RnQd8iMMUwXQEV1crFmQiQ`, 2026-08-15): **`pm:queue`**, split into two halves with different weights:

1. **The doc drift is mechanical and dispatchable now** (S): the `cartesianClickProps` doc line claims scatter / treemap / sankey are no-ops while all three have wired handlers, and says nothing that would warn about the derived-combo trap. Correct the comment to state what is actually wired, and name the #2945 derived-family consequence explicitly (adding a differently-familied series turns drill off). A doc-only truth fix, no behavior.
2. **Whether combo drills is a product question and is NOT ruled here** — the card is right that a combo click needs the same kind of semantic answer #4672's ruling gave the pivoted case (which series, which axis). That half stays recorded on this card and goes to the decision box only if dashboard usage ever surfaces a real pull; ⛔ no speculative wiring.

The sharp edge worth the record: **an author changing one series' `type` silently loses an interaction** — that is the AI-author silent-mismatch class this repo treats as first-class, which is why half 1 (making the contract statement true and the trap named) is queued rather than shrugged. Age-ordered priority.

Dispatch closeout + decision-box entry (PM session `session_01RnQd8iMMUwXQEV1crFmQiQ`).

The doc-truth half landed and merged as PR #4705: the `onChartClick` doc comment now states the measured wiring (scatter/treemap/sankey wired; radar and combo not), names the derived-family trap, and `AdvancedChartImpl.comboClickNoop.test.tsx` pins combo's current silence with a positive control. This card stays open for the remaining half, which is a product decision:

**Should a combo chart drill, and what does a click there mean?**

- **Option A — combo stays a no-op.** Status quo, now honestly documented and pinned. Close this card as recorded; the derived-family trap (adding `type: 'line'` to one series silently turns drill off chart-wide) remains a documented sharp edge.
- **Option B — wire mark-level clicks only (recommended).** Combo's marks are the same `Bar`/`Line`/`Area` components the drillable cartesian branch renders, and the item-level record-and-compose machinery from the #4672/#4682 ruling already stamps each mark's own series identity at the item handler — a mark click on a combo can emit `{category, categoryId, series, value}` with exactly the same semantics as on a plain chart, which also defuses the derived-family trap (drill survives a series changing mark type). Axis/surface clicks stay silent: on a multi-measure plot a surface click has no single series answer — the same reasoning the pivoted case's ruling used. Implementing this deliberately flips #4705's pin, which is what the pin is for.
- **Option C — Option B plus a designer-side hint** when a series-type edit derives `combo` (surfacing "this change turns the chart into a combo"), if the trap deserves an authoring-time signal beyond drill surviving.

Recommendation: **B**. The click machinery exists and is already series-correct at item level; the incremental surface is small and the semantics need no new invention. C's hint half can be its own follow-up card if wanted — it is designer territory, disjoint from the renderer.

No dispatch until ruled — `needs-user-decision`.

**Maintainer ruling — 2026-08-16: Option B.** Verbatim: 「4692 B」

`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`. Recorded by the PM session; the remaining half of this card is now execution, not a question.

## What is ruled

**Wire mark-level clicks on the combo branch only.** `ComposedChart`'s `Bar` / `Line` / `Area` marks emit `{category, categoryId, series, value}` with the same semantics the plain cartesian branch already gives, reusing the item-level series-identity machinery from the #4672 / #4682 ruling.

**Scope guards — all three are part of the ruling, not implementer discretion:**

1. ⛔ **Axis and surface clicks stay silent.** On a multi-measure plot a surface click has no single series answer. This is the same reasoning the pivoted case's ruling used; do not "improve" on it.
2. ⛔ **Option C is NOT ruled.** The designer-side hint when a series-type edit derives `combo` is disjoint from the renderer and belongs to a separate card if it is ever wanted. Do not add authoring-time signals in this dispatch.
3. ✅ **#4705's pin is meant to be flipped.** `AdvancedChartImpl.comboClickNoop.test.tsx` asserts combo's current silence; this work deliberately inverts it. Replace the assertion, keep the positive control, and keep a negative pin for the axis/surface path so guard 1 stays enforced. Also update the `onChartClick` doc comment #4705 corrected — it currently names combo as a no-op, which this change makes false.

## Four-lens analysis (#7498)

1. **Platform long-term coherence** — B removes a special case rather than adding one: six of seven cartesian branches drill today and *which branch a chart lands on is derived, not authored* (`effectiveChartFamily` resolves to `combo` when series families differ, per #2945). B also invents no semantics — it applies the series-identity answer #4672 already ruled to the rest of the family. Option A would make the derived special case permanent.
2. **Measured business pull** — deliberately **not** load-bearing here, and this is the lens most likely to be misread. The failure is silent: an author adds `type: 'line'` to one series, drill dies chart-wide, nothing errors and the authored spec never mentions `combo`. Silent failures do not generate pull signals — users do not report "my drill broke", they stop using drill. Absence of pull is not evidence of absence when the failure mode is invisible. (Contrast objectui#4662, where the failure *is* visible and silence therefore is evidence.)
3. **AI-agent error-resistance** — the decisive lens. A local, innocuous-looking spec edit silently removes an interaction from the whole chart: the silent-mismatch class this repo treats as first-class. #4705 made the trap *documented*, but documentation does not protect an author who never reads the source comment. B defuses it structurally — drill survives a mark-type change.
4. **Startup scope discipline** — mildly favours B, against the usual pull of this lens toward "do nothing". The maintained surface already exists (#4705's doc carve-out plus a pin asserting an inconsistency); B *reduces* it by deleting the carve-out, and its incremental code is small because the item-handler machinery is already built. C loses this lens outright: a new permanent designer surface with no demand signal.

## Dispatch note

The `repo:objectui` seat owns dispatch here. Age-ordered against that seat's queue — nothing in this ruling asks for it to jump the line.
